nodes.label: ADR-0021: packages/domain — the pure isomorphic domain layer
nodes.rationale: Eleven references already treat the package as load-bearing while domain behaviour accumulated in apps/api services and the login state machine was implemented twice with measurable drift. Web and RN must ship the same behaviour from the same slice (Law 7), which two hand-maintained state machines cannot satisfy.

nodes.label: packages/domain (pure isomorphic TypeScript)
nodes.rationale: May import nothing but the TypeScript standard library; never NestJS, React, RN, storage, fetch, env reads, packages/db, packages/ui or any app. Intended contents: shared formatters (formatInr, E.164 display), the invite/role invariants, and the login flow reducer.

nodes.label: domain is the BOTTOM layer (contracts → domain, never the reverse)
nodes.rationale: Owner ruling 2026-07-30 corrected an earlier draft that allowed contracts types: both mechanical gates had always contradicted the prose, and since the contracts tag already permits contracts → domain, sanctioning domain → contracts would have made the two packages mutually importable — a package cycle.

nodes.label: Business enums as pure TS unions at the bottom
nodes.rationale: A value both layers need is defined in domain and packages/contracts builds its z.enum from it — validation still belongs to contracts (Law 4) and the value still has exactly one definition.

nodes.label: Rules and catalogs are injected parameters, never module-level globals
nodes.rationale: The POC's resolveRules() singleton is the anti-pattern this rule exists to prevent.

nodes.label: dependency-cruiser domain purity rules
nodes.rationale: Inert until the directory existed, so a green cruise proved less than it appeared; proving them exposed that an unresolvable import is invisible to the cruiser (no dependency edge, so 'green' never proves 'nobody tried').

nodes.label: dependencyTypes ['npm'] misses devDependency imports
nodes.rationale: A react devDependency import passed clean until both purity rules were widened to ['npm','npm-dev']; the same hole existed in no-raw-http-clients (rule 20) and got the same widening.

nodes.label: The boundaries tag check is TRANSITIVE
nodes.rationale: Adding @heliogrid/domain to contracts turned pnpm boundaries red naming @heliogrid/ui — a package the change never touched — because ui allows contracts and turbo walks the whole graph. The ui tag was widened ahead of the slice so the next implementer does not meet a failure whose obvious readings are all false.

nodes.label: Ships dist/, not source
nodes.rationale: main/types/exports point at ./dist/ with no "type": "module" — with it, tsc emitted ESM that CJS NestJS could not require(). The earlier src entry survived only on pnpm's dev symlink layout: every gate stayed green while the built api/worker container would have died at require("@heliogrid/domain").

nodes.label: Duplicated login flow state machine (web vs RN drift)
nodes.rationale: Implemented twice with measurable behavioural drift — done-step dwell 1400ms vs 900ms, navigator.onLine vs local state for offline, and differently shaped failure unions.

nodes.label: The package lands empty of behaviour
nodes.rationale: Owner decision 2026-07-30: extracting a machine out of login screens the auth rebuild is about to delete is refactoring code with no future. Creating it now is still deliberate — the purity rules must not land at the same moment as the first behaviour they police.

nodes.label: Rejected: delete the eleven references instead
nodes.rationale: Cheaper today, but leaves the login drift with nowhere to go and every future flow repeating it.

nodes.label: Rejected: share via packages/contracts
nodes.rationale: Contracts is the wire format; putting behaviour there couples the API surface to client state machines.

nodes.label: Rejected: a shared component/renderer layer (react-native-web, Tamagui)
nodes.rationale: Conflicts with bare RN (ADR-0011) and with pixel fidelity to the design system; only decision logic is shared, platform concerns stay in the apps.

nodes.label: Rejected: wait for the auth rebuild and create it then
nodes.rationale: Would keep the purity rules inert through the router work and leave five CLAUDE.md files pointing at something that does not exist.

nodes.label: POC resolveRules() singleton anti-pattern
nodes.rationale: A module-level global for rules/catalogs is exactly what the injected-parameters rule exists to prevent.
